analysis.one_liner: Adani Enterprises is the Adani Group's incubator company - it builds new businesses (airports, roads, green/new energy, data centres, mining services) and spins them off once they mature.
analysis.whats_happening: The board meets on 28 October 2026 (about two weeks from now) to approve Q2 FY27 results. The June 2026 quarter (Q1 FY27) saw revenue up 50% YoY to ₹32,924 crore and a record EBITDA of ₹5,642 crore (+49% YoY), but the company still posted a net loss of roughly ₹1,160-1,460 crore (figures vary slightly by source) because of a one-off ₹2,644 crore charge tied to its $275 million settlement with the US Treasury's OFAC over Iran-sanctions violations in LPG imports made between late 2023 and mid-2025. Separately, the US Justice Department's criminal bribery indictment against Gautam Adani was formally dismissed with prejudice in August 2026, and the SEC closed its related civil case for an $18 million penalty without any admission of wrongdoing. In September 2026, Adani Airport Holdings raised about $1 billion from Temasek, BlackRock-managed funds, Alpha Wave Global and Premji Invest for a 5.54% stake.
analysis.plain_terms: Think of this company as a startup factory inside a large group - it has historically spun off Adani Wilmar, Adani Power, Adani Transmission and Adani Total Gas once those businesses matured, and today it's doing the same with airports, highways, new energy and data centres. The tension right now: the underlying businesses are growing fast (revenue and EBITDA both up roughly 50% in the June quarter), but the bottom line swung to a loss because of a large one-time US sanctions settlement charge, not because the businesses themselves got weaker. Separating 'the operating business is scaling' from 'the reported profit number looks bad' is the key thing to hold in your head here.
analysis.quarters: Operating profit (EBITDA) has climbed steadily: ₹3,710 cr (Mar-25) → ₹3,310 cr (Jun-25) → ₹3,307 cr (Sep-25) → ₹3,642 cr (Dec-25) → ₹3,731 cr (Mar-26) → ₹5,019-5,642 cr (Jun-26, figure differs between screener's 'operating profit' line and the company's own EBITDA release - the two track different items, so treat them as directionally consistent rather than identical). Net profit tells a messier story: ₹4,015 cr → ₹976 cr → ₹3,414 cr → ₹5,727 cr → -₹167 cr → -₹1,160/-1,462 cr over the same quarters. Management attributed the Jun-26 loss explicitly to the ₹2,644 crore OFAC exceptional charge, saying pre-tax profit excluding that item was a positive ₹1,295 crore. The cause of the smaller Mar-26 loss (-₹167 cr) was not independently verified here - check the company's exchange filing for the exact break-up before treating it as part of the same pattern.
analysis.performance_read: The stock closed at ₹2,722.6 on 14 October 2026, down 34.5% from its all-time high of ₹4,157.74 hit in December 2022. The only corporate action on record is a 2:1 stock split in December 2009 - no demerger shows up in this data, so unlike some other falls in this group's history, this drawdown is not an artifact of value moving into spun-off shares; it's a genuine price decline from the peak. Over 1 year the stock is up 8.2% versus Nifty's -10%, so it has outperformed recently; over 3 years it's up 12.2% versus Nifty's 14.7%, a mild underperformance; over 5 years it's up 65.7% versus Nifty's 23.4%, a large outperformance, though that window captures the recovery from the January 2023 Hindenburg-report crash. The last 3 months have been weak: -13.6% versus Nifty's -6.1%.
analysis.valuation_read: Trailing P/E is unusually high and inconsistent across sources - screener.in shows roughly 154x as of mid-October 2026, while another source cited around 57x as of late August 2026. Neither number is a clean read: trailing earnings are being dragged down by the two most recent loss-making quarters, so dividing price by a shrunken earnings base inflates the P/E mechanically rather than reflecting the market pricing in extraordinary growth. Price-to-book of 4.31x against a book value of ₹627/share is a steadier yardstick, and it is still rich given ROE of only 4.5-7.3% (latest versus 3-year average) and ROCE of roughly 5.8-6.6%. Why it might look expensive: reported earnings are near a trough because of one-off legal/settlement charges, not necessarily because the underlying businesses are worth less. Whether it actually IS expensive depends on how much the market is paying for future optionality in airports, data centres and new energy businesses that are still being built out - that judgment isn't verifiable from these numbers alone.
analysis.growth_read: The growth so far looks genuinely volume-led rather than margin or accounting trickery - both revenue (+50% YoY) and EBITDA (+49% YoY) rose together in the June 2026 quarter, driven by new businesses scaling (airport traffic, Ganga Expressway tolls starting, solar module capacity expansion, new data-centre orders) rather than a one-off reclassification. The flip side is that this is a company that keeps starting new, capital-hungry businesses instead of harvesting a mature one, so revenue growth doesn't yet show up reliably as profit growth.
analysis.health_read: Operating cash generation (EBITDA) is real and growing, but leverage is high: Debt/EBITDA of roughly 7.6x, Debt-to-equity near 1.2x, and screener flags a low interest coverage ratio; the current ratio of ~1.03 is tight. The dominant concern here looks like financial risk - leverage and capex intensity across several still-maturing businesses, and reliance on fresh capital raises (like the $1 billion airport stake sale) to fund growth - more than business risk in any single segment, since each segment's EBITDA has been expanding. Profits are not yet converting cleanly into free cash flow given this capex-heavy, incubator-stage model.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (the Adani family via S.B. Adani Family Trust and related entities) held about 74.8% as of June 2026, roughly unchanged from the prior quarter. Pledge is negligible at about 0.79% of promoter holding, and the promoter group has formally confirmed no fresh share encumbrance for FY26. One notable absence: GQG Partners, the global investor whose large stake purchase right after the January 2023 Hindenburg report was widely cited as a reputational vote of confidence, has been steadily exiting through 2026 - from about 10.8% in March 2026 down below the 1% disclosure threshold by June, and continuing to trim across Adani group holdings in the September quarter. SBI Mutual Fund has been the main domestic buyer absorbing GQG's sold stake.
strengths: Record Q1 FY27 EBITDA of ₹5,642 crore, up 49% YoY, on revenue up 50% YoY to ₹32,924 crore
Adani Airports drew $1 billion of third-party capital from Temasek, BlackRock-managed funds, Alpha Wave and Premji Invest for a 5.54% stake in September 2026 - external validation of that business
Major US legal overhangs have cleared: the DOJ criminal bribery indictment against Gautam Adani was dismissed with prejudice (August 2026) and the SEC case settled for $18 million
Promoter pledge is negligible (~0.79%) with no fresh encumbrance declared for FY26
watchpoints: Debt/EBITDA of roughly 7.6x and a flagged low interest coverage ratio - high leverage for businesses still in build-out mode
Trailing P/E of 57-154x depending on source is distorted by two consecutive loss-making quarters and isn't a reliable valuation signal right now
GQG Partners has cut its Adani Enterprises stake from 10.8% to below the 1% disclosure threshold through 2026 - a marquee post-crisis investor largely exiting
Q2 FY27 results on 28 October 2026 will show whether the OFAC-related charge was a one-off or whether further legal/settlement costs recur
analysis.one_thing: The 28 October 2026 Q2 FY27 results - specifically whether PAT turns positive again excluding exceptional items, confirming the June-26 loss was a one-time settlement charge rather than a weakening core business.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly revenue/EBITDA/PAT figures cross-checked between screener.in and multiple news reports of the company's own Q1 FY27 press release; these agree directionally but 'operating profit' (screener) and 'EBITDA' (company release) for Jun-26 differ (₹5,019 cr vs ₹5,642 cr) and were not reconciled. P/E (57x vs 154x) and ROCE (5.8% vs 6.57%) conflict across sources - both are reported here with the discrepancy flagged rather than averaged. The exact driver of the Mar-26 quarter's smaller net loss (-₹167 cr) was not independently verified - check the company's exchange filing on Screener. GQG and promoter shareholding figures are sourced from multiple shareholding-pattern aggregators (trendlyne, angelone) and news coverage of bulk deals, not the primary BSE/NSE shareholding disclosure filing itself.
